input.quote: 3.4 HDI's General Manager (as hereinafter defined), may upon no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Company, have the right to inspect the records of the Company's General Manager reasonably related to the calculation of such payments during the Company's normal business hours. The fees incurred by HDI in connection with the inspection shall be borne by HDI.
input.rationale: Section 3.4 is the only right of HDI to inspect Company records. It already satisfies several playbook elements: 30 days' prior written notice (better than the fallback's 15 days), inspection during normal business hours, a scope limited to payment-calculation records, HDI bearing its own inspection costs, and no right of access to Company systems. However, it contains no frequency limit, so HDI could inspect repeatedly at will; frequency ("no more than once per 12 months" / fallback "once per year") is a material term of both positions and unlimited audits are walk-away territory, so the clause fails the fallback. We therefore made the minimal edit adding a once-per-twelve-month cap. Two lesser points are noted but not flagged: the inspector is HDI's General Manager rather than an independent auditor, though § 8.2 already binds HDI to hold Company Confidential Information in strict confidence, and there is no underpayment-threshold cost shift, which is unnecessary since HDI bears its own costs in all cases.

proposal.summary: Cap HDI's records inspection right at once per 12 months.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have added a once-per-twelve-month cap on HDI's inspection right, consistent with our position that audits of our records be limited in frequency; the existing 30 days' notice, business-hours and HDI-cost terms are acceptable as drafted.

ops.newText: may, not more than once in any twelve (12) month period and upon no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Company,
